intro.title: Think like an investor
intro.body: Pick a real company from Lumi's market and reason your thesis with its data: what it does, why it could keep making money, its risks, whether it's expensive and how you'd manage the risk.
intro.p1: · 8 questions, about 15 minutes. Every step is saved.
intro.p2: · At the end: your thesis sheet, a score out of 100 and a certificate to share.
intro.p3: · +150 XP for your first thesis and +50 for the next ones (one a day).

project.lockedBody: This project opens when you pass «{needs}». It's the final challenge of the course's first section.
project.disclaimer: It's an exercise to learn how to analyse. Lumi doesn't tell you what to buy: the thesis is yours and you practise with virtual money.

pick.title: Pick a company
pick.body: Ideally one you know or whose products you use: it'll be easier to explain its business.
pick.placeholder: Search by name or ticker (Apple, ITX…)

s1.q: What does {name} do and how does it make money?
s1.help: Explain it as you would to a friend: what it sells, to whom and who pays it.
s1.label: Your answer
s1.ph: It sells… to… and makes money from…
s1.hint: If you can't explain it in two sentences, you don't understand the business yet. Read the description on the asset page and think about which part brings in the most money.

s2.q: Why could it still be making money in 5 years?
s2.help: Look for its edge over competitors: what others would find hard to copy.
s2.label: Explain why
s2.hint: A real advantage holds even if a richer competitor shows up. Ask yourself what would happen if someone sold the same thing cheaper tomorrow.
s2.hintNone: Admitting you don't see a clear advantage is good analysis too: then price and risk matter even more.

moat.BRAND: Brand: people prefer it and pay more for it
moat.NETWORK: Network effect: the more users, the more useful it is
moat.SWITCHING: Switching to another provider is costly
moat.SCALE: Size: what it does is expensive to replicate
moat.NONE: I don't see a clear advantage

s3.help: Write at least 2. Things that could make it earn less or make the share price fall a lot.
s3.label: Risk {n}
s3.ph0: For example: it depends heavily on a single product
s3.ph1: For example: it has a lot of debt and rates are rising
s3.ph2: For example: new regulation or a strong competitor
s3.count: {n, plural, =0 {No valid risks yet} one {# valid risk} other {# valid risks}} (at least 2)
s3.hint: Think in types of risk: competition, debt, regulation, dependence on one customer or product, currency and the price itself. Seeing only upsides is often confirmation bias.

s4.help: P/E is the share price divided by earnings per share: how many years of today's earnings you're paying. Compare it with its sector and its own history.
s4.compare: Its P/E is {ratio} times its sector's. Above 1, the market pays more for each euro of earnings than for its rivals.
s4.noSector: Not enough companies in its sector have data to compare. Reason it out with what you know about the business.
s4.noPe: We don't have this company's P/E. You can reason with its growth or earnings, or compare it with others you know.
s4.noHistory: We don't have its historical P/E in Lumi yet: if you know it, you can use it in your explanation.
s4.label: Why?
s4.hint: A high P/E doesn't mean expensive if earnings will grow a lot; a low one isn't a bargain if the business is getting worse. Watch out for anchoring: last year's price doesn't tell you whether it's expensive today.

s5.q: How much of your portfolio would you give it, and why?
s5.help: In the simulator. No single company should be able to sink your portfolio on its own.
s5.label: Weight in your portfolio
s5.inEur: With your simulated portfolio of {total}, that's about {eur}.
s5.concentrated: More than 10% in a single company is already quite concentrated.
s5.hint: Concentration rule: many investors put no more than 5-10% in a single company and never more than 20%. In the next step you'll see how much you risk with the 1% rule.

s6.q: Where would you put your stop and your target?
s6.help: The stop is the price at which you'd sell to cut the loss; the target is the price you think justifies your thesis.
s6.dist: The stop is {pct}% below the price.
s6.risk: With {w}% of your portfolio, if the stop is hit you'd lose {risk}% of your whole portfolio.
s6.riskHigh: More than 1%: lower the weight or move the stop closer.
s6.rr: What you could gain is {rr} times what you risk. Many look for at least 2.
s6.hint: Put the stop where your thesis would be wrong (for example below an important low), not where it "hurts a little". 1% rule: if it's hit, don't lose more than 1% of your portfolio.
s6.place: What you place on the chart
s6.chart: Weekly candles for the last year: tap or drag to place the level
s6.drag: Tap or drag on the chart to place the chosen level, or type the price below.

s7.q: How long would you hold it?
s7.help: A thesis about a business needs time to prove itself.
s7.label: Why that timeframe? (optional)
s7.hint: If your idea depends on the business, think in years. If you're thinking in weeks, it's more speculation than investing.

s8.q: What would make you change your mind?
s8.help: Decide now which facts would break your thesis, before the price makes you nervous.
s8.label: I'd change my mind if…
s8.ph: If it loses customers, if earnings fall two years in a row…
s8.hint: Write it with facts you can check (sales, margins, debt, a specific piece of news), not the price. That way you avoid the disposition effect: holding on to losers so you don't have to admit the mistake.

check.SHORT: Write a bit more: one or two sentences is enough.
check.RISKS_MIN: Write at least 2 risks (a few words each).
check.RISKS_SAME: The risks have to be different.
check.WEIGHT_MIN: Say how much of your portfolio you'd give it.
check.WEIGHT_MAX: No more than 20% of the portfolio in a single company.
check.NO_PRICE: We don't have this company's price right now. Come back in a while to set the stop and target.
check.STOP_ZERO: Say where you'd put the stop.
check.STOP_ABOVE: The stop has to be below the current price.
check.TARGET_BELOW: The target has to be above the current price.
check.INCOMPLETE: There's a step you haven't answered yet.

done.body: You've reasoned a complete thesis on {name}. That's how an investment is analysed: with data, risks and a plan.
done.simulator: Open the asset in the simulator
done.simulatorNote: If you like, practise your thesis with virtual money: you decide whether to trade and how much.

score.title: Your score, explained
score.completeHelp: 5 points for each step explained in some detail (3 if it's the bare minimum).
score.valuationHelp: Arguing with a figure or the P/E (5), in detail (5) and a conclusion consistent with its sector's data (5).
score.riskHelp: Weight up to 10%, 10 points (up to 20%, 5) and losing at most 1% of the portfolio if the stop is hit, 10 (up to 2%, 5).
score.planHelp: Possible gain of at least 2 times the risk (8; 1 time, 4), a horizon of a year or more (4) and what would change your mind, well explained (3).

cert.text: I've completed my investment thesis on {name} with Lumi.
